faq.q: What is the minimum investment required for SEBI's PRIM route?
faq.a: The minimum investment required to opt for the SEBI PRIM route is ₹25 lakhs. This makes it more accessible than traditional Portfolio Management Services (PMS), which typically require ₹50 lakhs.

faq.q: What types of instruments can a Portfolio Manager invest in under PRIM?
faq.a: Under PRIM, a Portfolio Manager is restricted to investing in mutual funds, Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), index funds, and Schemes of Investment Funds (SIFs). They cannot invest directly in individual stocks or bonds.

faq.q: Is the PRIM route regulated by SEBI?
faq.a: Yes, the PRIM route is fully regulated by SEBI. Portfolio Managers offering this service must be registered with SEBI and adhere to the SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020.

faq.q: How does PRIM differ from investing directly in mutual funds?
faq.a: PRIM involves professional management by a SEBI-registered Portfolio Manager who selects, manages, and rebalances your mutual fund portfolio. Direct investing requires you to manage all these aspects yourself.

faq.q: What are the typical fees associated with PRIM?
faq.a: Fees for PRIM generally include an annual management fee (a percentage of your AUM) and/or a performance-based fee (a percentage of returns above a certain benchmark). You should also factor in the expense ratios of the underlying mutual funds.

faq.q: Who is the ideal investor for the PRIM route?
faq.a: The PRIM route is ideal for high-net-worth individuals or affluent retail investors with at least ₹25 lakhs, who seek professional management for their mutual fund investments, prefer a hands-off approach, and value diversification and expert asset allocation.
